summary: Request-body sanitizer truncation causes upstream JSON parse exceptions and elevated 5xx rate
description:
Issue summary:
Customers (BrightWrite) and several internal synthetic monitors report a sudden increase in 5xx responses from the API gateway to model requests beginning ~2026-03-10 02:15 UTC. Error pattern shows upstream serving-runtime returning 500 with JSON parse errors.

Impact:
- Elevated 5xx rate (~6% of requests) for small- to medium-sized payloads (2KB–50KB) across streaming and non-streaming endpoints.
- Customer-facing failures for BrightWrite (dedicated) causing degraded UX and rate of retries.

Environment:
- prod cluster in us-east with cross-traffic mirrored to us-west for redundancy.
- Affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/stream.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Proxy a request with a large multipart JSON body that contains an embedded base64 payload and an additional custom header X-Client-Meta with long value (~2.5k characters).
2) Send the request through API gateway with request-size-sanitizer enabled (recent patch deployed 2026-03-09 23:40 UTC).
3) Observe 502/500 return from gateway or runtime with parse failures.

Observed behavior:
- The request-body sanitizer (middleware) truncates certain fields when combined header+body length exceeds an internal threshold. Truncation occurs without updating the Content-Length or properly terminating JSON boundary, producing malformed JSON forwarded to the runtime. The serving-runtime reports JSON parse exception and returns 500.
- Thundering retry loops from some clients amplify effective load causing additional upstream connection churn and ephemeral OOM spikes on a subset of GPUs.

Initial logs/snippets:
- apigw (2026-03-10T02:16:02Z) WARN request-sanitizer: "field_truncated=true header_length=2540 body_length=11234 threshold=13500" request_id=req_8fa3
- runtime (2026-03-10T02:16:03Z) ERROR json_parser: "unexpected end of input" model=redwood/rlhf-medium-1 request_id=req_8fa3 trace_id=tr_91b
- gateway (2026-03-10T02:16:05Z) ERROR proxy: "upstream returned 500" request_id=req_8fa3 upstream=runtime-12

Investigation notes so far:
- Change window: request-sanitizer rewrite merged 2026-03-09 23:40 (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/api/pull/4821). The sanitizer introduced a byte-aware truncation step intended to protect downstream runtimes from excessively large fields but did not append a truncation marker nor adjust Content-Length.
- Replays of customer payloads in staging with sanitizer disabled succeed and return correct model outputs. With sanitizer enabled, staged runtime returns same JSON parse exception.
- Correlated spikes align temporally with sanitizer rollout and aggressive client retry behavior from BrightWrite when they receive non-2xx.
- Affected subset of runtimes observed higher GPU memory fragmentation and occasional watchdog restarts after repeated malformed inputs (non-zero but small percentage).

Mitigation applied (temporary):
- 2026-03-10 03:10 UTC: rolled back request-sanitizer feature gate on prod API gateway fleets in us-east. Immediate drop in 5xx rate to baseline observed within 2 minutes.
- Advised BrightWrite to pause automated retries while rollback propagated.

Root cause hypothesis:
- Request-body sanitizer truncates large fields without adding a well-formed truncation token or adjusting Content-Length. As a result malformed JSON is forwarded to the serving-runtime which throws parse errors and occasionally triggers additional runtime instability under heavy retry churn.

Next steps / long-term fix:
1) Patch the sanitizer to either: a) add an explicit truncation marker that the runtime can interpret, or b) reject requests early with a 413/400 and clear reason. (Owner: ingress team)
2) Add unit/integration tests to simulate header+body edge cases across typical client SDKs.
3) Harden runtime JSON parsing to gracefully handle truncated input and early-return a 400 instead of propagating 500 under controlled circumstances.
4) Add telemetry: histogram of truncated-field occurrences, and an alert for sanitizer_truncate_rate > 0.1% by route.

Desired owner and ETA:
- Ingress middleware owner: Lena Ortiz. Patch target: 2026-03-12 for a non-breaking reject-mode fallback.
- Runtime defensive fix: Samir Gupta. Target: 2026-03-18.
comments: BrightWrite (customer): 2026-03-10 02:30 UTC - 'We're seeing repeated 500s from the /v1/generate route for requests that previously worked. Rate of failures ~5-7%. We're on a dedicated plan and this impacts production.'
Support (Maya Chen): 2026-03-10 02:45 UTC - Acknowledged, opening incident and escalating to ingress and runtime. Collecting sample request ids and asking customer to pause retries if possible.

Ingress (Lena Ortiz): 2026-03-10 03:05 UTC - We rolled back the sanitizer gate for us-east fleets at 03:10 UTC. Early metrics show 5xx rate returning to baseline. Reproduced malformed JSON on staging when sanitizer is enabled. Root cause likely in latest sanitizer rewrite. Linking PR 4821.

Runtime (Samir Gupta): 2026-03-10 03:20 UTC - Observed parse exceptions and a small number of GPU watchdog restarts correlated with malformed inputs. Implementing safer parse path to early-return 400 for truncated payloads as temporary mitigation.
Support (Ravi Patel): 2026-03-10 04:00 UTC - Notified BrightWrite of rollback and asked them to confirm service recovery; requested approval to run canary patch for sanitizer reject-mode in staging.
BrightWrite (customer): 2026-03-10 05:12 UTC - 'Confirming service recovered after your rollback. We'll hold off on retries until you notify us.'
SRE (Jasper Nguyen): 2026-03-11 09:10 UTC - Added dashboard tiles for "sanitizer.truncate.count" and alert rule to page when truncate rate exceeds 0.1% over 5m.
Ingress (Lena Ortiz): 2026-03-12 14:22 UTC - PR with reject-mode and test vectors created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/api/pull/4893. Requesting review and canary deploy schedule.
Support (Ravi Patel): 2026-03-13 11:05 UTC - Status updated: patch ready and scheduled for canary in us-east on 2026-03-13 18:00 UTC. Customer notified and tentative ETA for full fix 2026-03-18.
resolution: Temporary rollback of request-sanitizer gate restored baseline. Long-term fix in progress: ingress middleware will change truncation to explicit reject (413/400) and runtime will add defensive parse handling. Customer confirmed recovery.
resolution_notes: Rollback performed 2026-03-10 03:10 UTC. Canary patch PR created 2026-03-12. Monitoring and alerts added. Follow-up: post-deploy verification checklist and SDK guidance for clients to avoid aggressive retry windows when receiving 4xx/5xx during rollout.
